title: The forward pass and the KV cache
intro: Two tenants share GPU memory. One never moves. The other never stops growing.

steps.title: One token at a time
steps.body:
Generation is **autoregressive**: the model predicts one token, appends it, and runs again — each token conditioned on *all* previous ones. A 500-token answer = **500 full forward passes**.

Each pass: `tokens → embeddings → [attention + FFN] × N layers → LM head → next-token scores`. Nearly all parameters and compute live in seven **linear layers** per block (`q/k/v/o_proj` in attention, `gate/up/down_proj` in the FFN).

steps.title: Q, K, V — and why the past is cacheable
steps.body:
In attention, the current token's **Query** is scored against every previous token's **Key**; the softmaxed scores blend their **Values**. The crucial asymmetry: a new token needs the **K and V of every past token**, but only its *own* Q — and past K/V **never change**.

Recomputing them every step would be pure waste, so they're cached in GPU memory — at every one of the N layers, so the savings multiply by N.

steps.title: 320 KB per token adds up
steps.body: Per token you store K and V at every layer across the KV heads: `2 × layers × KV-heads × head-dim × bytes`. For Llama 3 70B that's 2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 ≈ **320 KB/token**. Innocent — until you multiply by context and users:

viz.title: One request's appetite
viz.caption: Drag to 128K: one request ≈ 40 GB — a third of the weights, per user.

steps.title: Where it all lives
steps.body:
**SRAM** (20 MB @ ~19 TB/s, beside the tensor cores) ← **HBM** (40–80 GB @ 1.5 TB/s, holds weights + cache) ← **CPU DRAM** (huge but ~12 GB/s away). Weights load into HBM once; the cache grows there per request; every step streams chunks of both into SRAM.

Now watch the cache fight for space — this is the machine a production server has to keep alive:

viz.title: The pressure vessel
viz.caption: 180 GB left after the weights. Raise users and context, then send in the whale.

recap: One token = one forward pass; K/V of the past are cached so only Q is fresh. ~320 KB/token on a 70B means context length is a **memory budget**. Weights are the fixed tenant, the KV cache the growing one — and speed is governed by HBM→SRAM data movement plus tensor-core math.
